name: Access brokerage
thesis: The hidden hand is often the person who determines who gets the meeting, which memo reaches the principal, who attends the committee and what receives follow-up.
evidenceFor: Published responsibilities for meeting, personnel and policy coordination
whatWouldProveMore: Calendars, routing records, decision memoranda and testimony showing repeated exclusion or prioritization changed outcomes.
boundary: Access can shape decisions without proving secret ownership of the decision-maker.

name: Agenda and information control
thesis: Power can operate before a formal vote through issue selection, briefing design, sequencing, classified information and the framing of available options.
evidenceAgainst: Decision-makers receive competing information and can request alternatives
Leaks, oversight and institutional rivalry disrupt control
whatWouldProveMore: Version histories, briefing books, attendee records and decision logs connecting framing choices to final outcomes.
boundary: Framing influence is not proof that every decision is manipulated.

name: Appointment and succession pipeline
thesis: The capacity to select, vet, promote, remove or nominate operators can outlast a single policy decision and reshape institutions over time.
evidenceFor: Dynastic succession and board nomination structures
evidenceAgainst: Confirmations, boards, legal qualifications and internal bargaining constrain appointments
whatWouldProveMore: Nomination records, vetting files, board minutes and longitudinal appointment networks.
boundary: Appointment influence must be tied to a lawful mechanism, not inferred from friendship or surname.

name: Permanent-state continuity
thesis: Professional bureaucracies, military commands, intelligence services, central banks, courts and regulatory systems preserve capacity, records and policy momentum when political leaders change.
evidenceFor: Statutory mandates, career services, treaty structures and standing committees
evidenceAgainst: Elected leaders can reform, direct or abolish functions within law
whatWouldProveMore: Career-network maps, implementation records, budget continuity and evidence of resistance or accommodation across administrations.
boundary: The permanent state is not automatically a single ideological 'deep state'.

name: Classified information asymmetry
thesis: Officials with access to intelligence, surveillance and secret operational reporting possess information ordinary voters, markets and many public officials cannot independently inspect.
evidenceAgainst: Oversight bodies and rival agencies create checks
whatWouldProveMore: Declassified records, oversight findings, lawful whistleblower evidence and authenticated operational directives.
boundary: Classified access is not proof of criminal conspiracy; serious claims require exceptional evidence.

name: Ownership and voting continuity
thesis: The most provable hidden continuity lies in voting pools, foundations, trusts, holding companies and family vehicles that preserve control while public executives change.
evidenceAgainst: Company power is bounded by jurisdiction, sector, finance and regulation
Ownership does not equal state authority
whatWouldProveMore: Beneficial-ownership records, shareholder agreements, trust instruments and voting outcomes.
boundary: This model is strongest at company level and weakest when inflated into universal control.

name: Networked oligarchy
thesis: A relatively small transnational class can exercise disproportionate influence through capital, boards, advisory roles, philanthropy, education and repeated institutional access without one formal headquarters.
evidenceFor: Documented board overlap, revolving-door careers and concentrated ownership
evidenceAgainst: Elites compete, sue, sanction and undermine one another
Common interests do not prove common command
whatWouldProveMore: Coordinated directives, shared governance, traceable joint decisions and outcomes not explained by aligned incentives.
boundary: Network position supports an influence hypothesis, not a unified conspiracy finding.

name: Single supreme human cabal
thesis: One concealed council commands governments, intelligence agencies, central banks, corporations and dynasties through a single chain of authority.
evidenceFor: No authenticated governance record currently establishes this model.
evidenceAgainst: Observed systems have distinct laws, rivalries, vetoes and conflicts
Existing councils have different memberships and mandates
whatWouldProveMore: Authenticated membership lists, command records, financial transfers, appointment instructions and independently corroborated operational evidence.
boundary: This remains a claim to test, not a conclusion to publish as fact.

name: Literal occult or non-human command
thesis: Baal, Moloch, Saturn, Lucifer or a Lightbringer intelligence literally directs modern institutions or named individuals.
evidenceFor: Religious, esoteric and testimonial traditions exist, but do not provide independently verifiable institutional command evidence.
evidenceAgainst: Symbolic resemblance and imagery cannot identify worship or command
whatWouldProveMore: Authentic direct records, independently verified practice and a demonstrable causal command chain—not visual similarity or anonymous testimony.
boundary: The site presents this as metaphysical or symbolic interpretation unless exceptional direct evidence emerges.
